heard: How does zip make a file three times smaller? It doesn't squeeze the letters, and it doesn't throw anything away. It does something sneakier. First, it hunts for repeats. In to be or not to be. The second to be is already in the file. So it deletes it and leaves a note. Go back 13, copy five. Those five letters took 40 bits. The note takes 14. But that's the small trick. The big one is hiding in the alphabet. In English, E shows up 172 times as often as Z. So why should both cost eight bits? Zip gives E just three bits and Z9. Common letters get cheap. Rare ones get expensive. Then it writes the code table at the top, so your computer can rebuild every letter exactly. That's how a page of English shrinks to a third, and not one letter is lost. Subscribe if you thought it just squeezed the letters.
